newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CRICKET-DALE PUTS QUEENSLAND IN CONTROL IN FINAL.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-DALE PUTS QUEENSLAND IN CONTROL IN FINAL.

text.p: Queensland pace bowler Adam Dale claimed six wickets for 38 as Western Australia sank into trouble on the second day of the Sheffield Shield final on Saturday.
Dale helped reduce the home side to 164 for nine at close of play at the WACA Ground, still 156 runs behind Queensland's first innings score of 320.
Western Australia number three Murray Goodwin saved his team from the follow-on with a gritty 63 before he became one of Dale's victims shortly before the close.

Queensland, who began the day on 266 for four, must win the five-day match to capture the Shield title while Western Australia need only avoid defeat because of their higher finish on the table at the end of the regular season.
Dale set the tone right from the off by removing openers Mike Hussey and Ryan Campbell cheaply, leaving Western Australia reeling at five for two early on.
Goodwin, who was overlooked by Western Australia selectors at the start of the season, managed to defy the visitors for 230 minutes, hitting nine fours before he was trapped leg before wicket.
The diminutive left-hander added 51 runs for the eighth wicket with fast bowler Jo Angel, who contributed 28 in a crucial partnership.
